title: Ephemeral backpressure synchronizer and cold-queue latency compensation
author: Jordan Lee
body: Motivation: We saw a recurring production pattern where tenants that hit the system after a cold window (KV cache misses + cold model kernels) caused short-lived latency spikes and oscillatory shedding across ephemeral worker pools. Root cause analysis showed two compounding effects: (1) backpressure signals were emitted immediately and independently by each worker which amplified bursts into synchronized shedding, and (2) the retry/priority re-enqueue logic over-reacted to transient queue lag, immediately reintroducing load and causing near-immediate re-shed. This PR implements a runtime-level synchronizer and a light-weight cold-queue latency compensation to reduce oscillation and stabilize SLOs during cold/ephemeral traffic patterns. Summary of changes: - Add ephemeral backpressure synchronizer that aggregates per-worker pressure signals over a sliding window and emits a smoothed, weight-adjusted control signal to the tenant prioritizer. The synchronizer sits in the serving runtime and is opt-in per capacity pool. - Introduce cold-queue lag compensation that applies a transient holdoff and staggered requeue policy for requests that experience kernel cold starts or KV cache misses; reduces immediate re-enqueue flood on transient latency events. - Add a new runtime metric set (runtime.backpressure.sync.*) and two Grafana dashboard panels for visualizing synchronizer state, hysteresis, and compensator effectiveness. - Integrate an e2e stress test that reproduces the cold-start oscillation pattern (integration/tests/backpressure_e2e.yaml) and add unit tests for timing edge cases. - Document behavior and knobs in docs/observability/backpressure.md and add a short operations runbook for toggling the feature per-pool or rolling it back. Rollout plan: feature is behind a per-pool runtime flag defaulted to OFF. Rollout sequence: 1) Canary on a small set of non-critical pools with observability enabled; 2) Monitor SLOs and dashboard for 72 hours; 3) Gradual ramp to additional pools if stable. Rollback plan: flip per-pool flag to OFF and allow workers to drain (no code rollback required). Testing & validation: included unit and integration tests, local perf bench harness added to benchmark-lab with deterministic cold-start traces, and a staging soak run for 48 hours. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for synchronizer logic and timing - [x] Integration e2e reproducer + regression assertion - [x] Added metrics and dashboard panels - [x] Ops runbook and rollback procedure - [x] Security review (no surface changes) Known limitations & follow-ups: - The synchronizer currently uses an in-memory aggregation. We'll follow-up to add a bounded, replicated option for multi-node pools (ENG-7220). - Some microsecond-level latency introduced by the smoothing window; measured <1ms p50 in benchmarks but will be monitored. Impact and rationale: this change reduces shed/retry oscillation, lowers observed p95/p99 latency spikes during cold windows, and keeps tenant SLOs more predictable without impacting steady-state throughput.
commits: feat(runtime): add ephemeral backpressure synchronizer and smoothing window
feat(runtime): implement cold-queue lag compensator and staggered re-enqueue
test(integration): add backpressure_e2e reproducer and regression assertion
docs(obs): add backpressure observability docs and ops runbook
bench: add deterministic cold-start traces to benchmark-lab harness
fix(tests): stabilize timing in synchronizer unit tests
review_comments: Aisha Kumar: Great isolation of signal aggregation — one question: can the smoothing window be tuned dynamically? Suggest a runtime knob and metric for window size.
Jordan Lee (author): Added a per-pool runtime knob (sync.window_ms) and exposed it as a metric. Updated docs to show recommended defaults for different pool sizes.
Tomás Álvarez: Integration test reproducer is helpful. I saw one flaky run due to clock skew in CI, recommended using a monotonic clock in the test harness.
Jordan Lee (author): Switched the test to the monotonic timer abstraction and re-ran CI — flakiness resolved.
Meera Shah: Ops runbook looks good; please add a dashboard alert for 'backpressure.sync.hysteresis_count' > 5 in 5m before full rollout.
Jordan Lee (author): Added the alert and an automated escalation note in the runbook.
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in ephemeral backpressure synchronizer and cold-queue lag compensation to reduce oscillatory load shedding during cold-start windows. Feature is off by default and controlled per-capacity-pool. Adds metrics and dashboards.
